items.quote: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
items.claim: In this text, Abraham tells his eldest servant, who ran his whole household, to put his hand under Abraham's thigh before swearing an oath.
items.action: asks for an oath gesture (hand under thigh)
items.mechanism: a physical gesture that goes with swearing an oath

items.quote: And I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:
items.claim: Abraham makes the servant swear by the LORD, God of heaven and earth, not to find a wife for his son among the Canaanite women, who are the people Abraham lives among.
items.action: makes the servant swear an oath banning marriage to a Canaanite
items.object: the servant; wife for his son
items.place: land of the Canaanites (where Abraham dwells)

items.quote: But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.
items.claim: Abraham orders the servant to go to Abraham's home country and relatives to find a wife for Isaac, which means marrying within the family group.
items.action: sends the servant to find a bride among his relatives
